### workspace library --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library list [--kind KIND] [--global | --builtin | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace library show REF [--global | --builtin | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace library info REF [--global | --builtin | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace library add PATH|- --kind KIND [--as NAME] [--link] [--force] [--project [NAME]] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace library update REF PATH|- [--link] [--project [NAME]] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace library remove REF [--yes] [--force] [--project [NAME]] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace library install REF [--name WS | --user] [--from global|project] [--force] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace library uninstall REF [--name WS | --user] [--force] [--dry-run] [--json]
       workspace library installed [--name WS | --user] [--kind skill|agent] [--json]

A store of named plays, prompts, recipes, agents and skills under $HOME/.config/workspace/library.
A play is a document an agent reads and follows; a prompt is short text sent as typed;
an agent is a Claude Code subagent file; a skill is a directory holding SKILL.md, and
`workspace start --agent/--skill` copies them into a new worktree. Entries are
global unless --project narrows them to one project; a project entry hides a global one
of the same name. REF is kind/name, or a bare name when one kind has it. `lib` is an
alias for `library`, and `workspace library` alone lists.

workspace ships built-in plays, the instruction packs binding, orchestrator, commits
and review (see `workspace instructions --help`). They can't be changed. --play and
show search them last, so a project or global play of the same name comes first there;
`instructions compose --pack` always uses the built-in one.

  list       List every library entry visible from here, sorted by kind then name
  show       Print a library entry's body
  info       Show a library entry's kind, scope, path, link target, description and modified time
  add        Copy a file or directory into the library
  update     Replace a library entry's content, or repoint its link
  remove     Delete a library entry or its link
  install    Copy a library skill or agent into a workspace's checkout
  uninstall  Delete the copy of a library entry that `library install` made
  installed  List the skills and agents installed from the library into a workspace's checkout or your home directory
Run `workspace library VERB --help` for a verb's options.

        --kind KIND                  agent, play, prompt, recipe, skill, spine or tmuxinator template (kind name: template) (add: required; list: a filter);
                                     add --kind recipe takes a YAML file of plays, packs, agents, skills, agent_kind and prompt, or of workflow and workflow_inputs (for 'start --recipe');
                                     add --kind skill takes a directory holding SKILL.md;
                                     add --kind spine takes a folder of plan-spine stage files (a template for 'spine init');
                                     add --kind template takes a folder holding project.yml and worktree.yml (a tmuxinator template set)
        --as NAME                    add: the entry name (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens)
        --link                       add, update: store a symlink to PATH instead of a copy
        --force                      add: replace an entry that has different content;
                                     install: replace a copy that has different content;
                                     uninstall: remove a copy that differs from the library entry
        --user                       install: copy to the user-level directory instead of a workspace;
                                     uninstall: remove the user-level copy
        --from STORE                 install: copy the entry of this store, global or project (default: the project's, else global)
        --yes                        remove: don't ask
        --global                     reads: only the global store
        --builtin                    reads: only the entries that ship with workspace
        --project, --name [NAME]     the project's store (NAME, or the project of the current directory);
                                     install, uninstall: the workspace to act on (default: the one of the current directory)
        --dry-run                    add, update, remove, install, uninstall: report what would happen and write nothing
        --json                       Print one JSON document (see docs/README.library.md)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library list    # see everything you can use from here: your project's entries, the global ones and the built-in packs
  workspace library show prompt/kickoff    # read back a prompt you saved, exactly as it will be sent
  workspace library info kickoff    # find out where an entry lives and whether it is a link, and whether it is the one `library show` prints
  workspace library add kickoff.md --kind prompt    # save a file as the global prompt kickoff, named after the file
  workspace library update prompt/kickoff kickoff.md    # replace the global prompt with the edited file
  workspace library remove prompt/kickoff    # delete a global entry, answering the question on the terminal
  workspace library install skill/write-tests    # give the workspace you are in a skill from the library
  workspace library uninstall skill/write-tests    # take a skill back out of the workspace you are in
  workspace library installed    # see which skills and agents the workspace you are in got from the library, and which you edited
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace library list --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library list [--kind KIND] [--global | --builtin | --project [NAME]] [--json]

List every library entry visible from here, sorted by kind then name.

Entries are global unless a project narrows them; a project entry hides a global one of the same
name. `workspace library` alone lists.

Options:
    --kind KIND                  Only this kind: agent, play, prompt, recipe, skill, spine or tmuxinator template (kind name: template)
    --global                     Only the global store
    --builtin                    Only the entries that ship with workspace
    --project [NAME]             The project's store (NAME, or the project of the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library list    # see everything you can use from here: your project's entries, the global ones and the built-in packs
  workspace library list --kind skill --global    # only the skills in the global store, e.g. before installing one
  workspace library list --builtin --kind play    # the packs that ship with workspace and that instructions compose can name
  workspace library list --kind prompt --json    # for a script: the same rows as one JSON document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace library show --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library show REF [--global | --builtin | --project [NAME]] [--json]

Print a library entry's body.

REF is kind/name, or a bare name when one kind has it. The body is printed as it is, so you can pass
it on, e.g. workspace start BRANCH --prompt "$(workspace library show prompt/kickoff)".

Options:
    --global                     Only the global store
    --builtin                    Only the entries that ship with workspace
    --project [NAME]             The project's store (NAME, or the project of the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library show prompt/kickoff    # read back a prompt you saved, exactly as it will be sent
  workspace library show kickoff    # the same with a bare name, when only one kind has an entry called kickoff
  workspace library show play/commits --builtin    # read a pack that ships with workspace before you rely on it
  workspace library show kickoff --json    # for a script: the entry and its body as one JSON document; a name nothing has exits 1 with unknown_library_entry
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace library info --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library info REF [--global | --builtin | --project [NAME]] [--json]

Show a library entry's kind, scope, path, link target, description and modified time.

REF is kind/name, or a bare name when one kind has it. effective says whether this entry is the one
`library show` prints; it is false when a project entry of the same name hides a global one.

Options:
    --global                     Only the global store
    --builtin                    Only the entries that ship with workspace
    --project [NAME]             The project's store (NAME, or the project of the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library info kickoff    # find out where an entry lives and whether it is a link, and whether it is the one `library show` prints
  workspace library info play/commits --builtin    # see the path and description of a built-in pack
  workspace library info skill/write-tests --global --json    # for a script: the global copy's details as one JSON document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace library add --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library add PATH|- --kind KIND [--as NAME] [--link] [--force] [--project [NAME]] [--dry-run] [--json]

Copy a file or directory into the library.

Copies PATH in (or links it with --link, or reads - from stdin with --as NAME). The name defaults to
the file name in kebab case; identical content is a no-op, different content under the same name
needs --force.

--kind recipe takes a YAML file of plays, packs, agents, skills, agent_kind and prompt, or of workflow and workflow_inputs (for 'start
--recipe'); --kind skill takes a directory holding SKILL.md; --kind spine takes a folder of
plan-spine stage files (a template for 'spine init'); --kind template takes a folder holding project.yml and
worktree.yml (a tmuxinator template set).

This writes to the library for real (the global store, or the project's with --project); --dry-run
says what would happen and writes nothing.

Options:
    --kind KIND                  agent, play, prompt, recipe, skill, spine or tmuxinator template (kind name: template) (required)
    --as NAME                    The entry name (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens)
    --link                       Store a symlink to PATH instead of a copy
    --force                      Replace an entry that has different content
    --project [NAME]             Add to the project's store (NAME, or the project of the current directory)
    --dry-run                    Report what would happen and write nothing
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library add kickoff.md --kind prompt    # save a file as the global prompt kickoff, named after the file
  workspace library add kickoff.md --kind prompt --dry-run    # check first: it reports added, unchanged or the refusal and writes nothing
  workspace library add kickoff.md --kind prompt --project    # keep it for the project of the current directory only
  workspace library add ~/Notes/playbook.md --kind play --link    # link a note, so edits to the note show up in the library at once
  workspace library add ~/Notes/spine-template --kind spine --as team --link    # keep a folder of stage files as a template for 'spine init'
  workspace library add - --kind prompt --as resume-note < resume.txt    # save text from stdin, which needs --as for the name
  workspace library add kickoff.md --kind prompt --force    # replace kickoff after you changed the file; without --force a different file under that name exits 1 with an error
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace library update --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library update REF PATH|- [--link] [--project [NAME]] [--dry-run] [--json]

Replace a library entry's content, or repoint its link.

REF is kind/name, or a bare name when one kind has it. The entry must already exist in the global
store, or in the project's with --project; this writes it for real unless --dry-run.

Options:
    --link                       Store a symlink to PATH instead of a copy
    --project [NAME]             The project's store (NAME, or the project of the current directory)
    --dry-run                    Report what would happen and write nothing
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library update prompt/kickoff kickoff.md    # replace the global prompt with the edited file
  workspace library update prompt/kickoff kickoff.md --dry-run    # see whether the file differs from the stored prompt: updated or unchanged, nothing written
  workspace library update kickoff kickoff.md --project    # replace the project's copy only, by bare name
  workspace library update play/playbook ~/Notes/new-playbook.md --link    # point a linked play at another note
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace library remove --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library remove REF [--yes] [--force] [--project [NAME]] [--dry-run] [--json]

Delete a library entry or its link.

Deletes the entry or its link from the global store, or the project's with --project, for real; the
source file is never touched. It asks first on a terminal. With --json it never asks, so pass --yes
or --dry-run. A tmuxinator template that a tmuxinator.template or tmuxinator.worktree_template key
selects is refused (template_in_use) unless --force, which removes it and warns which keys still name it.

Options:
    --yes                        Don't ask
    --force                      Remove a tmuxinator template a config key still selects
    --project [NAME]             The project's store (NAME, or the project of the current directory)
    --dry-run                    Report what would happen and write nothing
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library remove prompt/kickoff    # delete a global entry, answering the question on the terminal
  workspace library remove prompt/kickoff --dry-run    # see what would go before anything does
  workspace library remove play/playbook --yes    # delete a linked play without being asked, as a script must; the note it linked stays
  workspace library remove kickoff --project --yes    # delete the project's copy and let the global one show through again
  workspace library remove template/team --yes --force    # delete a tmuxinator template even though new configs are set to render from it
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace library remove --help --json
--- exit 0
--- stdout
{"usage":["workspace library remove REF [--yes] [--force] [--project [NAME]] [--dry-run] [--json]"],"description":"Delete a library entry or its link.\n\nDeletes the entry or its link from the global store, or the project's with --project, for real; the\nsource file is never touched. It asks first on a terminal. With --json it never asks, so pass --yes\nor --dry-run. A tmuxinator template that a tmuxinator.template or tmuxinator.worktree_template key\nselects is refused (template_in_use) unless --force, which removes it and warns which keys still name it.","options":[{"flags":"--yes","description":"Don't ask"},{"flags":"--force","description":"Remove a tmuxinator template a config key still selects"},{"flags":"--project [NAME]","description":"The project's store (NAME, or the project of the current directory)"},{"flags":"--dry-run","description":"Report what would happen and write nothing"},{"flags":"--json","description":"Print one JSON document"},{"flags":"-h, --help","description":"Show this help"}],"examples":[{"command":"workspace library remove prompt/kickoff","scenario":"delete a global entry, answering the question on the terminal"},{"command":"workspace library remove prompt/kickoff --dry-run","scenario":"see what would go before anything does"},{"command":"workspace library remove play/playbook --yes","scenario":"delete a linked play without being asked, as a script must; the note it linked stays"},{"command":"workspace library remove kickoff --project --yes","scenario":"delete the project's copy and let the global one show through again"},{"command":"workspace library remove template/team --yes --force","scenario":"delete a tmuxinator template even though new configs are set to render from it"}]}
--- stderr
--- end
### workspace library install --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library install REF [--name WS | --user] [--from global|project] [--force] [--dry-run] [--json]

Copy a library skill or agent into a workspace's checkout.

Copies to .claude/skills/NAME/ or .claude/agents/NAME.md unless library.install.skills_dir or
agents_dir says otherwise, as start --skill/--agent does for a new workspace: identical content is
unchanged, different content needs --force, a path the repo tracks is never overwritten; the copy is
listed in info/exclude. --user copies to your home-level directory instead
(library.install.user_skills_dir, user_agents_dir; ~/.claude/... by default). This writes files for
real; --dry-run reports what it would do and writes nothing.

Options:
    --name NAME                  The workspace to act on (default: the one of the current directory)
    --user                       Copy to the user-level directory instead of a workspace
    --from STORE                 Copy the entry of this store, global or project (default: the project's, else global)
    --force                      Replace a copy that has different content
    --dry-run                    Report what would happen and write nothing
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library install skill/write-tests    # give the workspace you are in a skill from the library
  workspace library install skill/write-tests --dry-run    # check what would be copied into this workspace's checkout and write nothing
  workspace library install agent/reviewer --name my-app    # give another workspace a subagent without leaving your directory
  workspace library install skill/write-tests --user    # make a skill available in every project, from your home directory
  workspace library install skill/write-tests --from global --force    # replace a copy you edited with the global entry, even where the project has its own
  workspace library install skill/write-tests --name my-app --json    # for a script: the outcome (installed or unchanged) as one JSON document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace library uninstall --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library uninstall REF [--name WS | --user] [--force] [--dry-run] [--json]

Delete the copy of a library entry that `library install` made.

Deletes the copy of REF that `library install` made in a workspace's checkout, or with --user from
the home-level directory. A copy that differs from the library entry needs --force; the library entry
and the info/exclude line stay. This deletes files for real; --dry-run reports and deletes nothing.

Options:
    --name NAME                  The workspace to act on (default: the one of the current directory)
    --user                       Remove the user-level copy
    --force                      Remove a copy that differs from the library entry
    --dry-run                    Report what would happen and write nothing
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library uninstall skill/write-tests    # take a skill back out of the workspace you are in
  workspace library uninstall skill/write-tests --dry-run    # see which copy would be deleted from this workspace's checkout
  workspace library uninstall agent/reviewer --name my-app    # take a subagent out of another workspace
  workspace library uninstall skill/write-tests --force    # delete a copy you edited, which would otherwise be refused
  workspace library uninstall agent/reviewer --user    # remove the copy from your home directory
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace library installed --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace library installed [--name WS | --user] [--kind skill|agent] [--json]

List the skills and agents installed from the library into a workspace's checkout or your home directory.

Reads a workspace's checkout (--name WS, default: the current directory's) or the user level
(--user); writes nothing. A copy counts when its name is a library entry's or the repo's
info/exclude lists it; modified = differs from that entry.

Options:
    --name NAME                  The workspace to act on (default: the one of the current directory)
    --user                       List the user-level copies
    --kind KIND                  Only skills or only agents
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace library installed    # see which skills and agents the workspace you are in got from the library, and which you edited
  workspace library installed --name my-app --kind skill    # only the skills of another workspace
  workspace library installed --user --json    # for a script: the copies in your home directory as one JSON document
--- stderr
--- end

play      handoff              builtin  Check context after every task and hand off to a fresh conversation before it runs out

play      notes                builtin  Read and write this workspace's working notes in its notes directory, never in the repo
play      orchestrator         builtin  Work as an orchestrator that delegates to sub-agents
play      plan-review          builtin  Review the workspace plan with reviewer sub-agents, write plan-review.md, and post the verdict to the inbox
play      promote              builtin  Move this checkout's work into a new workspace, seed it, start its agent, and stop working on it here

play      research             builtin  Research a goal and write the findings to a note in the notes directory, with no code changes
